checks.reason: Integrity, implementation assertions, native behavior and actual art/destination judgments remain separate; no human or broad milestone acceptance is inferred.
Checker disables bytecode, calls pure release inspection, and has no build/test/process/write path; redirection is a separate caller write.
Argparse supports documented flags; selected claims do not suppress release checks; status maps to exit 0/1/2.
Selected unittest module creates TemporaryDirectory fixtures; CLI/MCP/export subprocess vectors include -B; this suite does not call a host, browser or provider.
Packaging tests invoke live bundle build and knowledge tests invoke live knowledge build, so discovery is not an inspection route.
-B is described narrowly, not as suppression of application outputs or every child/tool write.
All three displayed readiness prepare/run/grade commands match their current argparse declarations, including --host/--setup/--python, timeout and fresh --output.
Prepare validates listed bundle bytes against its local manifest, creates external consumer/trial inputs and queries host/runtime; it does not prove canonical-current kit or model behavior.
Outer readiness runner can return normally after recording a nonzero native exit. Native completion status and separate grade are required; grade refuses an existing output.

Native-production prepare calls provider configure without a remote call; running the authorized assignment exposes official provider tools and can perform paid work. Local readiness assigns no provider/art work.
Named legacy report helpers call freeze and write fixed evidence files; check_host_evidence also performs temporary local replay.

Declared Node/browser/loopback workflow writes capture/check/import evidence; state writes and automatic acceptance are not implied. Installed consumer probe intentionally checks unavailable capability with missing Node.
Direct verifier/builder/wheel/benchmark main blocks invoke their mutating function without argument parsing, so --help is not a safe inspection command.

Archive precedes build-module imports; source/reference/knowledge/example work and first bundle precede tests; benchmark and second bundle precede distribution and final checked-input comparisons. Dated/current outputs described accurately.
Known-output archive covers explicit roots and current top-level evidence; it omits generated plugin NOTICE, build metadata and tool caches and does not roll back changes.

Normal completed failure returns 1 and records failed/not_run stages; run-directory creation is outside try and abrupt interruption or record-write failure may prevent a complete report. Guide preserves this limit.

Wheel check uses uv build/venv/pip in temporary locations with fresh production dependencies, then public installed/copied probes. Standalone main publishes wheel-check only after success and has no full-run archive.
Benchmark calls installed tiktoken encoding loaders; inspected local loader downloads on cache miss and writes configured/default cache. This is not a model/provider call.

Bundle build writes/copies manifests, requirements, runtime/resources/NOTICE and can remove unchanged obsolete generated entries. Other builders overwrite documented knowledge/examples/benchmark outputs without prior-output archives.
Old command/result sections remain history; current choices are distinct, and the guidance requires preserving failures, exact inputs and original grades when correcting evaluation.
